symptoms: Check engine light, rough idle, poor fuel economy
likely_causes: Vacuum leak, dirty mass airflow sensor, weak fuel pump
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for code P0171. 2. Perform visual inspection for vacuum leaks. 3. Check MAF sensor voltage. 4. Test fuel pressure.

symptoms: Check engine light, engine vibration, loss of power
likely_causes: Faulty spark plugs, worn ignition coils, low compression
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve code P0300. 2. Use oscilloscope to test coil outputs. 3. Inspect and replace spark plugs. 4. Perform compression test.

symptoms: Check engine light, reduced fuel efficiency
likely_causes: Clogged catalytic converter, faulty oxygen sensor
diagnostic_steps: 1. Confirm P0420 code. 2. Perform O2 sensor voltage test. 3. Check exhaust backpressure. 4. Inspect catalyst temperature.

symptoms: Check engine light, faint fuel odor
likely_causes: Loose or cracked fuel cap, broken EVAP hose
diagnostic_steps: 1. Verify P0455 code. 2. Inspect fuel cap and tighten/replace. 3. Perform smoke test on EVAP lines.

symptoms: Delayed gear engagement, whining noise
likely_causes: Leak in transmission pan gasket, worn seals
diagnostic_steps: 1. Check transmission fluid dipstick level and condition. 2. Inspect pan gasket and seals for leaks. 3. Top up fluid to proper level.

symptoms: Brake warning light, squeaking during braking
likely_causes: Brake pads worn beyond minimum thickness
diagnostic_steps: 1. Visual inspection of pad thickness. 2. Measure pad wear. 3. Replace pads if below spec.

symptoms: Engine cranks slowly, dim headlights, check battery light
likely_causes: Aged battery, corroded terminals, charging system fault
diagnostic_steps: 1. Measure resting battery voltage. 2. Perform load test. 3. Inspect and clean terminals. 4. Check alternator output.

symptoms: Clunking noise over bumps, poor steering feel
likely_causes: Age, harsh road impacts
diagnostic_steps: 1. Perform bounce test on front corners. 2. Inspect strut mounts for cracks or play. 3. Replace if excessive movement detected.

symptoms: Overheating, low coolant level, sweet smell
likely_causes: Hose degradation, loose clamp
diagnostic_steps: 1. Inspect radiator hoses for cracks or bulges. 2. Check clamp tightness. 3. Perform pressure test on cooling system.

symptoms: ABS warning light, brake pedal feel unchanged
likely_causes: Damaged wheel speed sensor wiring, faulty ABS module
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for ABS codes. 2. Inspect wheel speed sensor connectors for corrosion. 3. Test sensor resistance. 4. Replace module if no sensor fault.

issue_name: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
symptoms: Check engine light, rough idle, reduced fuel efficiency
likely_causes: Faulty sensor, wiring harness damage, loose connector
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0110 code. 2. Inspect sensor connector for corrosion. 3. Measure sensor voltage at idle (should be ~0.5-0.8V). 4. Replace sensor if out of spec. 5. Clear code and retest.

issue_name: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
symptoms: Check engine light, slightly higher emissions
likely_causes: Heater element failure, blown fuse, wiring short
diagnostic_steps: 1. Verify P0135 code. 2. Check fuse for O2 sensor heater circuit. 3. Perform resistance test on sensor heater (should be 2-5 ohms). 4. Replace sensor if heater resistance out of range. 5. Clear code.

symptoms: Cruise control failure, erratic speedometer, gear shift issues
likely_causes: Failed sensor, damaged wiring, poor ground
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0500 code. 2. Use multimeter to measure sensor voltage while rotating wheel (should vary smoothly). 3. Inspect wiring harness for damage. 4. Replace sensor if voltage is constant or out of range. 5. Clear code and test drive.

symptoms: Transmission warning light, erratic shifting, limp mode
likely_causes: TCM software glitch, internal failure, wiring issues
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0700 and related secondary codes. 2. Check TCM power and ground circuits. 3. Perform TCM reflash if software update available. 4. If fault persists, replace TCM. 5. Clear codes and perform road test.

symptoms: Stalling, loss of power, check engine light, rough acceleration
likely_causes: Throttle body carbon build-up, motor failure, wiring fault
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P2101 code. 2. Inspect throttle body for carbon deposits; clean if needed. 3. Test motor resistance (should be 5-7 ohms). 4. Check wiring continuity. 5. Replace throttle body if motor faulty. 6. Clear codes.

symptoms: Battery warning light, dimming lights, eventual dead battery
likely_causes: Worn alternator bearings, diode failure, voltage regulator issue
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P2500 code. 2. Measure alternator output voltage at idle (≈13.5-14.5V). 3. Check AC ripple with oscilloscope. 4. Inspect drive belt tension. 5. Replace alternator if output low or ripple high. 6. Clear code.

symptoms: Engine stalling, misfire, check engine light
likely_causes: Sensor failure, oil contamination, damaged wiring
diagnostic_steps: 1. Verify P3000 code. 2. Check sensor signal with oscilloscope (should be a clean waveform). 3. Inspect for oil leaks onto sensor. 4. Replace sensor if signal absent or erratic. 5. Clear code and test drive.

symptoms: ABS light on, loss of ABS functionality, pulsating brake pedal
likely_causes: Pump seal leak, motor burnout, contaminated brake fluid
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan ABS module for fault codes. 2. Inspect pump for fluid leaks. 3. Measure pump motor resistance (should be within spec). 4. Replace pump if motor open/short or fluid contamination present. 5. Bleed brakes and reset ABS module.

symptoms: Uneven ride height, rear sag, handling instability
likely_causes: Spring fatigue, overloading, corrosion
diagnostic_steps: 1. Measure rear ride height compared to manufacturer specs. 2. Visually inspect springs for cracks or deformation. 3. Replace rear coil springs if sag exceeds tolerance. 4. Re-torque suspension bolts to spec.

symptoms: Engine overheating, fan not engaging, coolant temperature spikes
likely_causes: Burned relay contacts, wiring short, control module issue
diagnostic_steps: 1. Check fan operation with engine at operating temperature. 2. Test relay by applying 12V to coil terminals; listen for click. 3. Measure voltage at fan power side when coolant temp high. 4. Replace relay if no click or no voltage. 5. Verify fan operation after replacement.

symptoms: Engine coolant temperature not reaching optimal, heater not blowing warm air, check engine light
likely_causes: Stuck open thermostat, low coolant level, faulty coolant temperature sensor
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0128 code. 2. Verify coolant temperature with infrared thermometer. 3. Perform thermostat flow test by removing and placing in hot water. 4. Check coolant level and sensor wiring.

symptoms: Rough idle, loss of power, engine vibration, check engine light
likely_causes: Faulty ignition coil, worn spark plug, fuel injector clog
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0301 code. 2. Inspect spark plug for wear or fouling. 3. Swap coil with another cylinder and see if code follows. 4. Perform compression test on cylinder 1.

symptoms: Check engine light, possible fuel odor
likely_causes: Loose or cracked EVAP hose, faulty gas cap
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0442. 2. Perform visual inspection of EVAP hoses and gas cap. 3. Use smoke machine to locate leak. 4. Replace defective hose or cap.

symptoms: Stalling at idle, rough idle, check engine light
likely_causes: Dirty IAC valve, faulty IAC motor, vacuum leak
diagnostic_steps: 1. Read P0505 code. 2. Remove IAC valve and inspect for carbon buildup. 3. Clean IAC with appropriate cleaner. 4. Test IAC operation with multimeter. 5. Check for vacuum leaks.

symptoms: Engine may not start, intermittent stalling, check engine light
likely_causes: Corrupted ECM software, poor grounding, water intrusion
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0606. 2. Verify battery voltage >12.4V. 3. Inspect ECM connectors for corrosion. 4. Reflash or replace ECM using dealer equipment.

symptoms: Gear stuck in neutral, inability to shift, check engine light
likely_causes: Faulty range sensor, damaged wiring, TCM issue
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0705 code. 2. Inspect sensor connector for damage. 3. Test sensor resistance with multimeter per service spec. 4. Replace sensor if out of spec.

issue_name: Hybrid Battery State of Charge Imbalance
symptoms: Reduced electric assist, warning light, decreased fuel economy
likely_causes: Failed battery module, imbalance in cell voltage, BMS fault
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0A20. 2. Use hybrid diagnostic tool to read individual module voltages. 3. Identify out‑of‑balance cells. 4. Replace faulty module or recondition battery.

symptoms: Hard start, poor acceleration, check engine light
likely_causes: Leaking regulator diaphragm, clogged fuel filter, faulty fuel pump
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P1380. 2. Measure fuel rail pressure with gauge. 3. Inspect regulator for external fuel seepage. 4. Replace regulator if pressure out of spec.

symptoms: Battery warning light, dimming lights, eventual battery drain
likely_causes: Internal regulator failure, wiring short, blown fuse
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P2503. 2. Test alternator output voltage at idle and 2000 rpm. 3. Check regulator wiring and fuse. 4. Replace alternator if regulator output is abnormal.

symptoms: Engine knocking, rough idle, higher emissions
likely_causes: Clogged EGR passages, stuck closed valve, vacuum leak
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0401. 2. Remove EGR valve and inspect for carbon buildup. 3. Clean passages with appropriate solvent. 4. Test valve actuation with vacuum pump or electrical test.

issue_name: Mass Air Flow Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
symptoms: Check engine light, rough idle, reduced fuel efficiency
likely_causes: Dirty MAF sensor, cracked intake hose, wiring short
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0101 code. 2. Inspect intake hose for cracks or leaks. 3. Disconnect MAF sensor and measure voltage output while cranking. 4. Clean MAF sensor with appropriate cleaner. 5. Reinstall and clear codes, then test drive.

symptoms: Engine stalling, hard start, loss of power
likely_causes: Faulty sensor, damaged wiring, timing belt slip
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0340 code. 2. Visual inspection of sensor connector and harness for corrosion. 3. Measure resistance of sensor (compare to spec). 4. Use oscilloscope to verify signal while cranking. 5. Replace sensor if out of spec and clear codes.

symptoms: Engine may not start, dim headlights, check engine light
likely_causes: Weak battery, poor alternator output, loose battery terminals
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0562. 2. Measure battery voltage with engine off (should be >12.4V). 3. Start engine and measure voltage at battery terminals (should be 13.5‑14.5V). 4. Inspect and clean battery terminals and grounds. 5. Test alternator output load test if voltage low.

symptoms: Engine overheating, fan not engaging, check engine light
likely_causes: Failed relay, blown fuse, wiring short
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P2180 code. 2. Locate fan relay and check fuse. 3. Swap relay with identical known-good unit. 4. Test fan operation with engine at operating temperature. 5. Inspect relay control circuit for continuity.

symptoms: Rough idle, increased emissions, occasional stalling
likely_causes: Clogged EGR valve, carbon buildup, stuck actuator
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0402. 2. Remove EGR valve and inspect for carbon deposits. 3. Clean valve with appropriate cleaner. 4. Reinstall and clear code. 5. Perform road test to verify resolution.

symptoms: Intermittent stalling, random loss of power, check engine light
likely_causes: Corroded ECU connectors, water intrusion, failed ECU
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0666. 2. Inspect ECU connector pins for corrosion or damage. 3. Perform voltage check on ECU power and ground circuits. 4. If pins and voltage are good, consider ECU reflash or replacement. 5. Clear codes and perform functional test.

symptoms: Gear selector stuck, no gear changes, transmission warning light
likely_causes: Faulty range sensor, damaged wiring harness, poor connections
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0706. 2. Locate range sensor and inspect connector. 3. Test sensor resistance according to service manual. 4. Verify continuity of wiring harness. 5. Replace sensor if out of spec, then clear codes.

issue_name: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
symptoms: Check engine light, slightly higher fuel consumption
likely_causes: Heater element failure, wiring short, blown fuse
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P1345. 2. Locate O2 sensor bank 2 sensor 2. 3. Test heater circuit voltage with engine off and running. 4. Inspect fuse related to O2 heater circuit. 5. Replace sensor if heater is open circuit.

issue_name: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Low Input
symptoms: Steering feels heavy, intermittent loss of power assist, warning lamp
likely_causes: Faulty pressure sensor, hydraulic leak, electrical fault
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P1234. 2. Check power steering fluid level and look for leaks. 3. Measure sensor output voltage at low and high steering torque conditions. 4. Inspect wiring harness for damage. 5. Replace sensor if output out of spec.

symptoms: Throttle lag, unexpected acceleration, check engine light
likely_causes: Motor failure, carbon buildup, wiring short
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P2102. 2. Perform throttle body visual inspection for carbon. 3. Test motor resistance per service manual. 4. Apply 12V to motor terminals to verify movement. 5. Clean throttle body, replace motor if no movement, then clear codes.

symptoms: Check engine light, fuel odor, failed emissions test
likely_causes: Loose fuel cap, cracked vapor hose, faulty purge valve
diagnostic_steps: 1. Verify Check Engine Light is stored. 2. Perform EVAP leak test with smoke machine. 3. Inspect fuel cap and vapor lines for damage. 4. Test purge valve operation with multimeter.

symptoms: Rough idle, reduced fuel economy, increased emissions
likely_causes: Clogged EGR passages, stuck EGR valve, vacuum leak
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0410 code. 2. Remove and inspect EGR valve for carbon buildup. 3. Perform vacuum test on EGR control circuit. 4. Measure EGR flow with a flow meter if available.

symptoms: Multiple warning lights, intermittent engine stall, loss of power
likely_causes: Damaged wiring harness, faulty ECU, poor ground connections
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve all stored codes. 2. Inspect ECU connectors for corrosion. 3. Test continuity of communication wiring. 4. Perform ECU power and ground voltage checks.

issue_name: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
symptoms: Check engine light, poor fuel efficiency, increased emissions
likely_causes: Faulty O2 sensor heater, open circuit, blown fuse
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0141 code. 2. Check fuse for O2 sensor circuit. 3. Measure voltage at sensor connector while engine is warm. 4. Replace sensor if heater voltage is absent.

issue_name: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Malfunction
symptoms: Engine stalls, no start, intermittent loss of power
likely_causes: Damaged sensor, wiring short, faulty PCM
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0325 code. 2. Visual inspection of sensor and wiring. 3. Test sensor resistance with multimeter. 4. Verify signal with oscilloscope during cranking.

issue_name: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
symptoms: Check engine light, slightly higher fuel consumption
likely_causes: Contaminated O2 sensor, exhaust leak before sensor
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P2199 code. 2. Inspect exhaust for leaks upstream of sensor. 3. Perform live data read of O2 sensor voltage. 4. Replace sensor if voltage remains stuck.

issue_name: Turbocharger Boost Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Input
symptoms: Loss of power, reduced boost, check engine light
likely_causes: Faulty boost sensor, vacuum leak, damaged wiring
diagnostic_steps: 1. Confirm P0219 code. 2. Inspect sensor and vacuum lines for damage. 3. Measure sensor voltage at idle and under boost. 4. Replace sensor if voltage does not change appropriately.

issue_name: Internal Control Module Memory Checksum Error
symptoms: Engine may not start, multiple error codes, erratic performance
likely_causes: Corrupted ECU firmware, voltage spikes, faulty ECU hardware
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve all codes. 2. Check battery voltage and charging system stability. 3. Perform ECU reflash or replace if necessary. 4. Verify absence of power surges in vehicle wiring.

symptoms: Rough running, loss of power, increased fuel consumption
likely_causes: Faulty spark plug, bad coil, low compression
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0302 code. 2. Inspect and replace spark plug and coil on cylinder 2. 3. Perform compression test on cylinder 2. 4. Verify fuel injector operation.

symptoms: Stalling on idle, erratic throttle response, check engine light
likely_causes: Faulty TPS, damaged wiring, dirty throttle body
diagnostic_steps: 1. Verify P0120 code. 2. Check TPS connector for corrosion. 3. Measure TPS voltage range (0.5V closed to 4.5V open). 4. Clean throttle body and replace TPS if out of spec.
